name: GGLearn
description: Tracks, levels, competitions, certificates, admin and deploy.

cards.subject: GGLearn
says: is the company training academy for the brands
lets a learner pick a track and climb 20 levels from Novice to Titan
was rebuilt from the TrialTest and SkillsTest exam platforms into a learning product
cards.use: need the name of the product that trains staff across the brands
not: is a public marketplace that sells third-party courses

cards.subject: A track
says: is one question-bank domain
belongs to exactly one brand
is the unit a learner joins to study one subject
cards.use: need the unit a learner enrols in to study one subject
not: holds a single exam question

cards.subject: A brand
says: has a slug, a name and a tagline
is the grouping that a set of tracks hangs off
sits above tracks in the content hierarchy
cards.use: need to know what a group of tracks belongs to
not: is one learner's account

cards.subject: A track kind
says: is one of subject, product, service, tool, technology or process
labels what sort of thing a track teaches
is set on the track and not on individual questions
cards.use: want to classify a track by what it teaches
not: is one of beginner, intermediate or advanced

cards.subject: An enrolment
says: joins one learner to one track
is unique per user and track
stores the goal the learner chose and the level they were placed at
cards.use: need the record that links a learner to a track
not: is created by an exam run

cards.subject: A knowledge item
says: is the single source of truth for a track's content
is the row that authored questions link back to
has a version that rises when its body changes
cards.use: need the record that a question's facts come from
not: is issued as a certificate when a level is passed

cards.subject: A question type
says: is one of mcq, open or scenario
decides how an answer is graded
is stored on every question beside its level and prompt
cards.use: want to know what shape of question a learner will see
not: is one of easy, medium or hard

cards.subject: A study guide
says: shows the level syllabus plus flip cards from that level's questions
is stored in the lessons table
counts as one of the three daily quests when read
cards.use: want to revise a level before sitting its exam
not: is graded and can pass a level

cards.subject: A legacy foundations track
says: is hidden from browsing once a matching titan track exists
keeps working for enrolled learners and direct links
is not deleted when it is hidden
cards.use: wonder why an old TrialTest-imported track no longer appears in the list
not: is deleted when a titan track for the same subject is seeded

cards.subject: The legacy bank
says: is thin at levels 16 to 20
has no brand-specific content
is imported from the TrialTest data folder by the base seed
cards.use: wonder why real brand knowledge has to be authored by hand
not: covers every level of every brand in depth

cards.subject: The level ladder
says: runs from Novice at level 1 to Titan at level 20
has twenty named steps
includes Practitioner, Expert, Master and Legend among its names
cards.use: need the name of the full climb a learner makes in a track
not: has ten levels from Beginner to Master

cards.subject: A rank
says: groups four consecutive levels together
is one of Initiate, Adept, Expert, Master or Titan
decides which avatar a learner shows
cards.use: want to name a band of four levels
not: groups ten levels together

cards.subject: The Initiate rank
says: starts at level 1
runs from Novice to Beginner
cards.use: want the rank a brand-new learner starts in
not: starts at level 5

cards.subject: The Adept rank
says: starts at level 5
begins at Trainee and ends at Capable
cards.use: want the rank that covers levels 5 to 8
not: starts at level 9

cards.subject: The Titan rank
says: starts at level 17
covers Virtuoso, Legend, Grandmaster and Titan
cards.use: want the top rank, covering levels 17 to 20
not: starts at level 13

cards.subject: An exam run
says: draws 10 questions for the level
favours questions the learner has not yet answered correctly
is reused if an unfinished one already exists for that level
cards.use: need one attempt at a level exam
not: draws a fixed set of 20 questions every time

cards.subject: The pass mark
says: is 80 percent
unlocks the next level when reached
is applied to a weighted score and not a plain count
cards.use: want the score a run needs to pass a level
not: is 60 percent

cards.subject: Level unlocking
says: lets a learner start a level up to one above the highest level passed
means levels are taken in order
cannot be skipped by clicking ahead
cards.use: wonder whether a learner can jump straight to level 12
not: opens every level as soon as the learner enrols

cards.subject: The placement check
says: is a binary search for what someone already knows
probes the middle level with 3 multiple-choice questions each round
counts a level as mastered only when all 3 are answered correctly
never skips past level 15
cards.use: want a new learner to start above level 1 without sitting every exam
not: awards certificates for the levels it skips

cards.subject: A placed level
says: is stored on the enrolment
is only ever raised
never counts as passing for required learning or promotion
cards.use: need to know why a placement result does not satisfy a requirement
not: is lowered when a learner fails an exam

cards.subject: Multiple-choice grading
says: compares the answer with the stored option key after trimming and lowercasing
scores 1 for a match and 0 otherwise
returns the question's hint or 'Not quite.' as feedback
cards.use: want to know how an mcq answer is marked
not: is marked by Claude against a rubric

cards.subject: Open-answer grading
says: is done by Claude against a reference answer and a rubric
applies to the open and scenario question types
returns a score from 0 to 1 with one or two sentences of feedback
cards.use: need to know who marks a written answer
not: compares the typed text with an option key

cards.subject: The AI grader
says: wraps the learner's answer as untrusted data
cuts the answer to 4000 characters
is told never to follow instructions inside the answer
uses a model that the GRADER_MODEL setting can override
cards.use: worry that a learner could write instructions inside an answer
not: trusts the learner's answer as part of its own prompt

cards.subject: The keyword fallback
says: is used when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set or the AI call fails
measures coverage of words in the model answer and the rubric
never awards more than 0.9
cards.use: have no AI key configured but still need written answers scored
not: awards full marks when any keyword appears

cards.subject: The weight of a question
says: defaults to 10
multiplies the question's score when the run is totalled
makes some questions count for more than others
cards.use: want a harder question to count more toward a run score
not: is the number of seconds allowed to answer

cards.subject: A run score
says: multiplies each question's score by its weight
is the sum of those results divided by the total weight
passes at 0.8 or more
cards.use: work out how a run's final score is built
not: is the plain count of correct answers out of ten

cards.subject: A question in review
says: is held back from learners until it is published
is the status that imported company questions arrive with
is published for a whole track by an admin
cards.use: need new company questions kept hidden until their facts are checked
not: is already drawn into exams

cards.subject: A retired question
says: is taken out of the pool so it is no longer drawn
can be set back to active by a manager
is chosen from the improvement loop when a question is flawed
cards.use: need to stop a broken question from being asked without deleting it
not: is deleted from the database for good

cards.subject: The duplicate-prompt index
says: blocks the same prompt at the same track and level
is a unique index on the questions table
is why importing a file twice does not add duplicates
cards.use: see why re-running an import does not double the questions
not: stops a learner seeing the same question twice

cards.subject: A drill
says: is 5 instant-feedback multiple-choice questions
draws only from levels the learner has already passed
never draws from the level the learner is about to sit
cards.use: want quick practice that cannot leak exam answers
not: is a full level exam that can pass a level

cards.subject: A drill's answer record
says: notes which drill questions were really answered
uses a one-hour window
must reach enough distinct questions before XP is awarded
cards.use: see why opening a drill without answering earns nothing
not: awards XP the moment the drill page opens

cards.subject: The daily quests
says: are study the guide, quick drill and take an exam
can each be completed once per track per UTC day
feed streaks and badges
cards.use: want the three small daily tasks a learner can do
not: reset at the learner's local midnight

cards.subject: The quest XP values
says: give 20 XP for the study guide
give 30 XP for a quick drill
give 40 XP for finishing an exam
cards.use: need the points each daily quest is worth
not: give 100 XP for each quest

cards.subject: Exam XP
says: is the score times 100, rounded
adds 50 if the run passed
cards.use: work out the XP from a single exam run
not: is a flat 150 whatever the score

cards.subject: A streak
says: counts consecutive days with at least one quest
may end today or yesterday and still be live
cards.use: want to count days in a row of practice
not: counts only days with a passed exam

cards.subject: XP per level
says: is 150 on the rival scale
turns XP into a level by division
cards.use: need the exchange rate between XP and a level
not: is 100 XP per level

cards.subject: A rival
says: is a stable named opponent for every track
earns between 55 and 70 XP a day with a small wobble
has a level equal to its XP divided by 150
is deterministic, so no background job is needed
cards.use: want the opponent shown head-to-head on a track page
not: is another learner chosen at random

cards.subject: The On Fire badge
says: is earned by a 3-day streak
cards.use: wonder which badge marks three days in a row
not: is earned by passing level 10

cards.subject: The Unstoppable badge
says: is earned by a 7-day streak
cards.use: wonder which badge marks a week in a row
not: is earned by a 3-day streak

cards.subject: A competition
says: is a time-boxed contest on one track
is won by gaining a set number of levels before the deadline
can last from 1 to 90 days with an optional delayed start
cards.use: want learners to race each other on a track
not: is an exam with a time limit per question

cards.subject: A contest baseline
says: is the highest level passed before racing started
means only newly passed levels count
lets beginners and experts compete fairly
cards.use: wonder why a veteran does not win just by already being high
not: is level 0 for everyone

cards.subject: A reduced target
says: applies to someone within N levels of Titan
is shown on the leaderboard
stops the goal asking for levels that do not exist
cards.use: see why a person near the top has a lower goal than N
not: applies to anyone who started at level 1

cards.subject: Contest ranking
says: puts whoever reached the goal first on top
then orders by levels gained
uses XP in the window as the last tie-break
cards.use: work out who wins when two people both reach the goal
not: is decided by total XP first

cards.subject: Contest standings
says: are computed on read and clamped to the end time
never change once a contest has finished
cards.use: wonder why a finished leaderboard stays fixed
not: are rewritten each night by a job

cards.subject: A bot
says: is simulated and labelled as such
follows a fixed daily XP schedule
does not study or answer any questions
cards.use: need an opponent when nobody else is racing
not: is a trained model that sits real exams

cards.subject: Bot pace tiers
says: run at 45 XP a day for casual
run at 75 XP a day for steady
run at 120 XP a day for fierce
cards.use: set how fast a simulated opponent should move
not: run at 150 XP a day for every bot

cards.subject: A private contest
says: gives outsiders a 404
can only be opened by the organiser, invited people and members
hides even that it exists, with a generic page title
cards.use: keep a team race out of sight
not: can be watched by anyone without signing in

cards.subject: A public contest
says: can be watched by anyone without signing in
needs a consent tick before joining
can be switched to private but never the other way round
cards.use: want an open leaderboard that outsiders can follow
not: is hidden from every non-member

cards.subject: A level certificate
says: is issued automatically on passing level 5, 10, 15 or 20
is verifiable at /cert/ followed by its code
is titled Foundation, Practitioner, Expert or Titan
cards.use: need proof that a learner passed a milestone level
not: is claimed by hand after a contest ends

cards.subject: A contest certificate
says: is claimed after a contest ends
goes only to people who reached the goal
calls the first to finish champion and the rest finisher
cards.use: want a certificate for winning a race and not for passing a level
not: is issued automatically on passing level 10

cards.subject: The admin role
says: can offboard anyone except themselves
alone can publish a track's questions held in review
can override a promotion block with a reason
cards.use: need the role with the widest powers
not: is redirected to the dashboard from /admin

cards.subject: The manager role
says: can issue invites and run onboarding
can offboard only learners
can retire or restore a question
cards.use: need a role that runs people but cannot offboard other admins
not: can publish a whole track held in review

cards.subject: The learner role
says: is sent back to the dashboard if it opens /admin
can tick its own onboarding checklist items
cards.use: need the role that studies but does not manage
not: can issue invites

cards.subject: A job role
says: drives a person's recommended and role-required tracks
is matched in lower case, exactly
is free text on the person and not a pick-list
cards.use: see why a mistyped role gets no role-required tracks
not: is the same thing as the admin, manager or learner role

cards.subject: An invite
says: is a single-use link bound to one email address and job role
expires after 7 days
is the only way an account is created
cards.use: bring a new person into GGLearn
not: lets anyone self-register from the login page

cards.subject: An invite token
says: is random and shown once
is stored only as a SHA-256 hash
cannot be recovered by an admin later
cards.use: wonder why an old invite link cannot be shown again
not: is stored in plain text so it can be resent

cards.subject: Accepting an invite
says: needs a name and a password of 8 to 200 characters
consumes the invite and creates the account in one transaction
enrols the new person in up to 6 recommended tracks and gives them a checklist
cards.use: see why one link cannot create two accounts
not: needs a one-time code sent by email

cards.subject: Password storage
says: uses scrypt with the cost parameters kept inside the hash
upgrades a legacy hash at the next sign-in
cards.use: wonder how stored passwords are protected
not: keeps passwords encrypted with a key that can decrypt them

cards.subject: The login rate limit
says: allows 5 failed tries per IP and email pair
allows 30 per IP, both in 15-minute windows
lives in process memory and resets on restart
cards.use: wonder how repeated bad passwords are slowed down
not: is stored in the database and survives restarts

cards.subject: The session cookie
says: is signed and httpOnly
lasts 30 days and is enforced on the server
is invalidated by a per-user session version
cards.use: wonder how a sign-in is remembered
not: holds the password so the learner can be re-checked

cards.subject: The session version
says: is bumped to sign a person out everywhere
is bumped when someone is offboarded
makes older cookies stop working at once
cards.use: need to kill every live session for one person
not: is stored in the cookie and cannot be changed

cards.subject: Offboarding
says: sets the status to offboarded
ends access immediately by bumping the session version
adds a four-item offboarding checklist
is refused for the manager's own account
cards.use: need a leaver's access removed at once
not: deletes the person's history

cards.subject: The onboarding checklist
says: has five items for staff and three for customers
can be ticked by the new person for their own items
can be ticked for anyone by a manager
cards.use: see what a new joiner has to do in their first weeks
not: is ticked only by a manager

cards.subject: Sign-in method
says: is email and password only
has no single sign-on
is not backed by a mailer in the code
cards.use: wonder how people sign in to GGLearn
not: supports SSO through the company identity provider

cards.subject: A login's timing
says: pays for a password hash even for unknown or offboarded accounts
means response time does not reveal which emails exist
cards.use: worry that login time could reveal which emails have accounts
not: returns instantly for emails that are not registered

cards.subject: A scope
says: is a company, a brand or a project that a person belongs to
is set at invite time
decides which tracks a person can see
cards.use: need to define which part of the company someone works in
not: is a job role

cards.subject: An audience
says: is staff or customer for a person
is staff, customer or both for a track
keeps customers from seeing staff tracks
cards.use: see why a customer never sees a staff-only track
not: is the same thing as a scope

cards.subject: A shared brand
says: makes its tracks visible to all staff
includes academy brands such as Tech Foundations
cards.use: wonder why every staff member sees the technology tracks
not: is visible only to customers

cards.subject: A project-scoped track
says: is visible only to people with that project's scope
is stricter than a brand-scoped track
cards.use: keep a track limited to one project's staff
not: is visible to everyone in the company

cards.subject: The mandatory tier
says: must be passed by everyone in scope
is a tier on the track
cards.use: make a track compulsory for everyone
not: applies only to people whose job role matches

cards.subject: The role tier
says: is required for the job roles listed on the track
applies to everyone in scope if the roles field is empty
matches the person's job role exactly
cards.use: make a track compulsory for one job role
not: is compulsory for everyone in the company

cards.subject: The growth tier
says: is optional
is the default tier for a track
feeds promotion steps and not compliance
cards.use: mark a track as nice to have
not: is compulsory with a deadline

cards.subject: Required level and due days
says: default to level 5 and 30 days
are set per track at /admin/paths
start the clock from the first enrolment
cards.use: set how far and how fast a required track must be passed
not: default to level 20 and 7 days

cards.subject: The soft gate
says: blocks nothing
shows what is due on the dashboard
makes /admin/compliance list who is overdue
cards.use: wonder whether being overdue locks a person out
not: blocks sign-in when a deadline passes

cards.subject: Required learning
says: is counted only from real exam passes
leaves out tracks too thin to reach the required level
is synced at joining, at login and when scopes or policy change
cards.use: see why a placement result does not satisfy a requirement
not: is satisfied by a placement guess

cards.subject: A customer account
says: is invited like staff with the audience customer
gets the brands or projects they bought as scope
sees only customer or both tracks
cards.use: give a client access to getting-started material
not: sees every staff track in its brand

cards.subject: A career ladder
says: is one per job role
is a set of numbered rungs
starts people at level 1
cards.use: see the promotion path for a role
not: is a single track with 20 levels

cards.subject: A career step
says: is a pair of a track slug and the level to pass
belongs to one rung of a ladder
is skipped if the track is outside the person's scope
cards.use: express what a rung asks of a person
not: is a free-text task ticked by a manager

cards.subject: The three career measures
says: are Knowledge, Delivery and Communication and leadership
describe what a manager should see at each level
are the same for every company
cards.use: describe the dimensions of a role level
not: are Skill, Speed and Seniority

cards.subject: A career overlay
says: adds steps one company wants to the shared ladders for its own tracks
is stored under content/careers/overlays
cards.use: add a company-specific step without editing the shared role file
not: replaces the shared ladder for that company

cards.subject: A career bridge
says: lets someone cross from one ladder to another
names a from-role, a from-level and a to-level
can be chained to make a longer route
cards.use: plan a move such as Lead Developer into Engineering Manager
not: promotes the person automatically

cards.subject: A sub-level
says: is computed and never stored
is .0, .1 or .2 depending on how many of the next level's passable steps are met
is shown like L2.1
cards.use: see why a person reads as L2.1
not: is stored when a manager promotes someone

cards.subject: A promotion
says: is a manager's decision recorded in the promotions table
is allowed when every passable step is met and required learning is not overdue
cards.use: wonder who decides when someone moves up a rung
not: happens automatically once the steps are met

cards.subject: A career goal
says: is a role and level a person can reach plus a date
is set at /journey
can be removed by the person
cards.use: state where you want to be and by when
not: is assigned by a manager

cards.subject: The journey planner
says: finds the shortest route through ladders and bridges
spreads dates across the route
compares the pace needed with levels passed in the last four weeks
cards.use: turn a career goal into a dated plan
not: decides whether the person is promoted

cards.subject: A question mix
says: is the share of exam questions per domain for a role and rung
is shown on /journey as out of every 100 questions
drifts from a start mix toward a top mix as people climb
cards.use: see what a role will be asked
not: is the same for every role

cards.subject: A domain
says: is one of technology, tool, process, product, service, brand or leadership
is decided for a track by its kind unless domains.json overrides it
is the unit the question mix is spread over
cards.use: work out which part of the mix a track counts toward
not: is a company or brand

cards.subject: The import:knowledge script
says: loads knowledge items and their questions from JSON files
is idempotent, matching an item by track and title
can set study guides with a lessons key
cards.use: load authored questions for a company track
not: wipes the track before loading

cards.subject: A review-status import
says: saves questions as unpublished
is set with status review in the file
waits for an admin to publish at /admin/review
cards.use: load company questions without making them live
not: publishes questions as soon as the file is imported

cards.subject: The seed:ai script
says: builds the AI technology tracks from their card files
publishes questions immediately, not held for review
creates the facebook-marketing-titan and lead-generation-titan tracks
cards.use: load generated technology tracks
not: holds generated questions for review

cards.subject: The import:questions script
says: imports from the separate questions repository
dedupes and maps difficulty onto 20 levels
adds duplicates at shifted levels if run again on a track that has questions
cards.use: bring in a track from the questions repo
not: is safe to re-run on any track

cards.subject: The generate:bank script
says: authors questions with Claude from a track's knowledge items
runs a second blind pass to audit every answer key
saves questions as review unless told to activate
needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
cards.use: write questions for a company track that cannot be computed
not: is used for subjects with executable oracles

cards.subject: Dynamic questions
says: are built fresh from a seed each time
have answers worked out in code
are saved as one-off snapshot rows that never enter stored pools
cards.use: make an exam that is never the same twice
not: are stored in the bank and reused

cards.subject: A track's reach
says: is the highest level a person can pass
stops at the first level with no questions
counts as every level for tracks with dynamic generators
cards.use: see why a track with a gap at level 7 caps out below it
not: is the number of enrolled learners

cards.subject: A material change
says: asks everyone enrolled before the change to read the change within 7 days
is recorded with before and after text
does not rewrite linked exam questions
cards.use: tell learners that a policy or moto changed
not: rewrites every linked question automatically

cards.subject: A wording fix
says: is recorded in the change log
asks nobody to re-read the text
cards.use: correct a typo in company knowledge without bothering learners
not: asks everyone enrolled to re-confirm

cards.subject: A card track
says: is one JSON file of cards under content/cards
is expanded by the engine into about 20 multiple-choice questions per card
is checked with check:cards
cards.use: author a track from short facts
not: is a list of finished questions with no engine step

cards.subject: The production site
says: is served at gglearn.gglink.co.uk
sits behind Apache with TLS from certbot
reverse-proxies to the app on 127.0.0.1:3400
cards.use: need the address of the live GGLearn
not: is served directly by Next.js on port 80

cards.subject: PM2
says: runs the app as gglearn-web
restarts the app if memory passes 400M
starts the app with next start on port 3400
cards.use: need the process manager that keeps the app up
not: builds the app on the server

cards.subject: The Node 20 limit
says: means Node 21+ APIs such as Map.groupBy must be avoided
is why better-sqlite3 stays on a version with a Linux Node 20 prebuild
cards.use: decide whether a new JavaScript API can be used
not: lets any current Node feature be used

cards.subject: The deploy.sh script
says: rsyncs the code to the server
excludes node_modules, .next, .git, database files and .env files
installs, pushes the schema, builds and reloads PM2
cards.use: ship the latest code to production
not: pushes a Docker image to a registry

cards.subject: The schema push
says: runs drizzle-kit push without --force
fails the deploy on a destructive change
avoids deleting rows when a NOT NULL column is added to a table with data
cards.use: see why a risky schema change stops a deploy
not: runs with --force to guarantee success

cards.subject: The deploy health check
says: polls the local port up to 10 times, 3 seconds apart
fails the deploy unless it gets HTTP 200
prints the PM2 error log on failure
cards.use: need to know whether a deploy came back healthy
not: passes as soon as PM2 starts

cards.subject: The deploy workflow
says: runs on every push to main
can also be started manually
needs the secrets DEPLOY_SSH_KEY, DEPLOY_HOST, DEPLOY_USER and DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS
cards.use: see what ships code automatically
not: deploys only on tagged releases

cards.subject: The Cloudflare allow-list
says: lets only Cloudflare and the machine itself reach the site
is regenerated by update-cloudflare-ips.sh
keeps X-Forwarded-For from being spoofed around Cloudflare
cards.use: stop visitors bypassing Cloudflare
not: blocks Cloudflare and allows direct traffic

cards.subject: The TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS setting
says: defaults to 2 for Cloudflare plus Apache
decides how far from the end of X-Forwarded-For the real client sits
cards.use: fix rate limiting that sees the wrong client address
not: is the number of app servers behind the proxy

cards.subject: The SESSION_SECRET setting
says: must be at least 16 characters
signs every session cookie
signs everyone out when it is changed
cards.use: keep sessions valid across restarts
not: is optional in production

cards.subject: The ANTHROPIC_API_KEY setting
says: is optional
turns on AI grading of open and scenario answers
enables generate:bank
cards.use: enable AI marking
not: is required to start the app

cards.subject: The database
says: is SQLite in data/gglearn.db for local development
is excluded from the deploy rsync
should move to Postgres before multi-user production use
cards.use: wonder where learner data lives
not: is overwritten on every deploy

cards.subject: The /admin page
says: runs the question-improvement loop
flags questions that are nearly always failed or never failed
lets a manager review or retire a flagged question
cards.use: improve the question bank using real results
not: lists who is overdue

cards.subject: /admin/people
says: onboards people and issues invites
shows checklists and handover notes
offboards leavers
cards.use: bring someone in or take someone out
not: sets tier and deadline per track

cards.subject: /admin/paths
says: sets tier, audience, level and deadline per track
is where a track is made mandatory or role-required
cards.use: make a track required for a role
not: lists the people who are overdue

cards.subject: /admin/compliance
says: shows who is overdue on required learning
shows how many required tracks each person has done
cards.use: see who has not done what is required
not: promotes people

cards.subject: /admin/careers
says: is where managers record promotions
lets admins edit ladders
cards.use: promote someone or change a ladder
not: sets which tracks are mandatory

cards.subject: /admin/freshness
says: records a change to company knowledge
shows who has and has not read each change
cards.use: tell people the brand moto changed
not: retires a flawed question

cards.subject: /admin/review/[slug]
says: is where an admin approves a track's questions held in review
enrols the people the track applies to when approved
cards.use: make imported company questions live
not: is open to every learner

cards.subject: A product backlog
says: is the ordered list of work a product team may do next
is reordered as priorities change
cards.use: need one place to see all candidate work
not: is the list of released features

cards.subject: A product roadmap
says: shows the direction of a product over time
communicates intent rather than a fixed delivery promise
cards.use: explain where the product is heading to stakeholders
not: lists every task a developer must do

cards.subject: Acceptance criteria
says: state the conditions a piece of work must meet to be accepted
are written before development starts
cards.use: agree what done looks like for a story
not: are written by testers after release

cards.subject: A definition of done
says: is a shared checklist that applies to every piece of work
covers things like tests, review and documentation
cards.use: keep quality consistent across all stories
not: differs for every story

cards.subject: A feature flag
says: switches a feature on or off without redeploying
lets a release be separated from a launch
cards.use: release code but hold back the feature
not: permanently removes a feature

cards.subject: A staged rollout
says: exposes a change to a small share of users first
limits the damage of a bad release
cards.use: reduce the risk of shipping to everyone at once
not: ships to all users in one step

cards.subject: An activation metric
says: measures whether a new user reaches the first moment of value
is more telling than sign-up counts
cards.use: judge whether onboarding works
not: counts total registered accounts

cards.subject: Cohort retention
says: tracks a group of users who started in the same period
shows whether later cohorts stay longer than earlier ones
cards.use: see if product changes improved stickiness
not: averages all users together

cards.subject: Retrieval practice
says: strengthens memory by recalling material instead of rereading it
is the reason quizzes help learning
cards.use: choose between rereading notes and testing yourself
not: is rereading the same notes several times

cards.subject: Spaced practice
says: spreads study over several days
usually beats cramming for long-term retention
cards.use: plan revision for something to be remembered next month
not: packs all study into one night

cards.subject: Mastery learning
says: asks a learner to meet a standard before moving on
matches a pass mark that unlocks the next level
cards.use: stop weak foundations from carrying forward
not: lets learners skip any level

cards.subject: Formative assessment
says: checks understanding during learning so it can be corrected
is low-stakes feedback and not a final grade
cards.use: give feedback while learning is still under way
not: is a final exam that certifies

cards.subject: Summative assessment
says: judges what was learned at the end
can award a pass or a certificate
cards.use: decide whether someone has met the standard
not: is a quick practice drill

cards.subject: Item difficulty
says: is the share of test-takers who answer a question correctly
flags a question nearly everyone fails as possibly flawed
cards.use: decide if a question is too hard or too easy
not: is how long the question text is

cards.subject: A distractor
says: is a wrong option that should look plausible
is weak if nobody ever chooses it
cards.use: judge the quality of the wrong options in a multiple-choice question
not: is the correct answer

cards.subject: Test validity
says: is whether a test measures what it claims to measure
is not guaranteed by a high pass rate
cards.use: wonder whether an exam measures job skill
not: is the same as consistency across attempts

cards.subject: Test reliability
says: is how consistent a test's results are across attempts
does not by itself prove the test measures the right thing
cards.use: wonder whether a test gives repeatable results
not: is whether the test covers the right topics

cards.subject: A rollback
says: returns production to a previous known-good version
should be rehearsed before it is needed
cards.use: recover quickly from a bad release
not: rewrites the version history

cards.subject: A health check
says: tests that a service answers correctly after a change
can fail a deploy automatically
cards.use: know a service came back up
not: measures traffic volume

cards.subject: Idempotency
says: means running an operation again leaves the same result
makes seed scripts safe to repeat
cards.use: design a script that can be run twice safely
not: means an operation fails the second time

cards.subject: A backup restore test
says: proves a backup can actually be restored
is the real check that a backup works
cards.use: trust a backup before you need it
not: confirms a backup file exists

cards.subject: Least privilege
says: gives each person or process only the access it needs
limits the damage from a stolen credential
cards.use: decide what access a new role needs
not: gives everyone admin access for convenience

cards.subject: Rate limiting
says: caps how often a client may attempt an action
slows credential guessing
cards.use: slow brute-force attacks on login
not: encrypts the data in transit

cards.subject: Expand and contract
says: splits a risky schema change into additive and removal steps
keeps old and new code working during the change
cards.use: change a database column without breaking running code
not: drops the old column first

qa.q: How many levels does a learner climb in a GGLearn track, and what is the last level called?
qa.right: 20 levels, ending at Titan
wrong: 10 levels, ending at Master
20 levels, ending at Legend
15 levels, ending at Expert
qa.why: The ladder runs from Novice at level 1 to Titan at level 20.

qa.q: What pass mark does a level exam need?
qa.right: 80 percent
wrong: 50 percent
60 percent
100 percent
qa.why: A run passes at 0.8 or more and unlocks the next level.

qa.q: How many questions does one exam run draw for a level?
qa.why: Each attempt draws 10 questions for the level.

qa.q: Which table holds the single source of truth for a track's content?
qa.right: knowledge_items
wrong: lessons
runs
certificates
qa.why: Authored questions link back to a knowledge_items row.

qa.q: How does a person get a GGLearn account?
qa.right: A manager or admin issues a single-use invite link bound to their email
wrong: They register themselves from the login page
They sign in with the company single sign-on
They are created when a track is seeded
qa.why: Account creation is invite-only and there is no SSO.

qa.q: Which levels issue a certificate automatically?
wrong: Every fifth level and every contest win
Only level 20
qa.why: Level certificates are issued on passing levels 5, 10, 15 and 20.

qa.q: What is a drill?
qa.right: Five instant-feedback multiple-choice questions drawn from levels already passed
wrong: A ten-question exam that unlocks the next level
A timed contest against a bot
A study guide with flip cards only
qa.why: A drill draws only from levels the learner has passed, so it cannot reveal exam answers.

qa.q: Which three things are the daily quests?
qa.right: Study the guide, a quick drill and take an exam
wrong: Pass a level, join a contest and read an update
Log in, set a goal and invite a colleague
Take a placement check, a drill and a contest
qa.why: They are worth 20, 30 and 40 XP.

qa.q: How many XP equal one level on the rival scale?
qa.why: A rival's level is its XP divided by 150.

qa.q: What happens to the access of someone who is offboarded?
qa.right: It ends at once and a four-item offboarding checklist is added
wrong: It ends at the end of the month
It continues until they sign out
Their account and results are deleted
qa.why: Offboarding sets the status and bumps the session version so access ends immediately.

qa.q: Where is the production site served from?
qa.right: gglearn.gglink.co.uk, reverse-proxied by Apache to a PM2 app
wrong: A serverless platform with an edge cache
A Docker Swarm cluster behind a load balancer
A desktop app installed on each laptop
qa.why: Apache terminates TLS and proxies to gglearn-web on 127.0.0.1:3400.

qa.q: What kinds can a track be?
qa.right: Subject, product, service, tool, technology or process
wrong: Beginner, intermediate or advanced
Staff, customer or both
Mandatory, role or growth
qa.why: Those are the six track kinds.

qa.q: Which sign-in method does GGLearn use?
qa.right: Email and password only
wrong: Single sign-on with the company directory
Magic links sent by email
A shared team password
qa.why: There is no SSO.

qa.q: A new starter was invited a week ago but never opened the link. What is true of it now?
qa.right: It has expired, because an invite lasts 7 days
wrong: It still works because invites never expire
It works once more after an admin reactivates the account
It turns into a customer invite
qa.why: An invite fails if used or expired.

qa.q: A learner passes 7 of 10 questions on a level exam. What follows?
qa.right: The run fails, because the pass mark is 80 percent
wrong: The run passes and the next level opens
The run passes with a warning
The run is discarded and not recorded
qa.why: Seven of ten is below 0.8, and the score is also weighted.

qa.q: A learner wants to start level 9 after passing only level 5. What happens?
qa.right: They cannot; they may start only one level above the highest passed
wrong: They can start any level they choose
They can start it if they have a drill streak
They can start it after a manager signs off
qa.why: Levels unlock in order.

qa.q: A learner places at level 6 in the placement check, then sees the same requirement show as not done. Why?
qa.right: A placement result never counts for required learning; only real exam passes do
wrong: Placement results expire after a day
Placement only counts for customers
The requirement needs a manager sign-off first
qa.why: Compliance and promotion use levels earned by real exams.

qa.q: No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set. How are open answers scored?
qa.right: By a keyword-coverage fallback that never awards more than 0.9
wrong: They all score zero
They score full marks automatically
They wait in a queue for a manager to mark
qa.why: Without a key, or if the AI call fails, the fallback is used.

qa.q: Why does a drill never include questions from the level about to be sat?
qa.right: So that practice cannot reveal exam answers
wrong: Because those questions are not yet written
Because drills are limited to level 1
Because drills are timed and exams are not
qa.why: Drills draw only from levels already passed.

qa.q: Two people reach their competition goal. Who ranks higher?
qa.right: Whoever reached it first
wrong: Whoever has more XP in total
Whoever started at a lower level
Whoever joined the contest last
qa.why: Ranking is goal reached first, then levels gained, then XP in the window.

qa.q: What does a contest baseline stop?
qa.right: A veteran winning only because they were already at a high level
wrong: A learner joining two contests
A bot beating a human
A contest running longer than 90 days
qa.why: Only levels newly passed after the baseline count.

qa.q: A private contest is opened by someone who is not a member. What do they see?
qa.right: A 404, so the contest's existence is not revealed
wrong: A read-only leaderboard
A login prompt naming the contest
A request-to-join button
qa.why: Outsiders get a 404 for private contests.

qa.q: Who pays the prize for a GGLearn contest?
qa.right: The organiser, who also records it
wrong: GGLearn, from the academy balance
The winner's manager automatically
The brand's finance system via a webhook
qa.why: GGLearn never holds or moves money.

qa.q: What does the soft gate mean for a person with an overdue required track?
qa.right: Nothing is blocked, but compliance shows them as overdue
wrong: They are locked out until they pass
Their account is offboarded
They are demoted a rung
qa.why: Required learning never blocks work.

qa.q: A job role is typed as 'Social Media Mgr' while the track says 'social media manager'. What follows?
qa.right: The role-required track does not match, because job roles are compared exactly in lower case
wrong: It matches because spelling is fuzzy
The admin is emailed to fix it
Every role-required track is assigned instead
qa.why: Job roles are free text matched exactly.

qa.q: A manager wants to publish all of a track's questions held in review. What happens?
qa.right: Only an admin can do that
wrong: Any learner can do it
It publishes itself after 7 days
A manager can do it from /admin
qa.why: activateTrackQuestions is admin only.

qa.q: Where do you record that the brand moto changed so staff re-read it?
qa.right: /admin/freshness
wrong: /admin/people
/admin/careers
/cert
qa.why: A material change asks everyone enrolled before the change to read it.

qa.q: A deploy fails because the app did not return HTTP 200. What did the script do?
qa.right: Polled the local port 10 times, 3 seconds apart, then failed
wrong: Rolled the database back automatically
Restarted Apache and tried again
Sent an email to the team
qa.why: The health check fails the deploy and prints the PM2 error log.

qa.q: A drill is opened but no questions are answered. How much XP does it earn?
qa.right: None, because XP needs enough distinct questions actually answered
wrong: 20 XP for opening it
30 XP, the drill value
5 XP per question shown
qa.why: The server records which drill questions were really answered.

qa.q: A learner has an exam run with score 0.9 that passes. What is the exam XP?
qa.why: Exam XP is the score times 100, rounded, plus 50 if passed.

qa.q: A schema change adds a NOT NULL column to a table with rows. Why does the deploy fail rather than proceed?
qa.right: drizzle-kit push is run without --force, so a destructive change stops it
wrong: The lock refuses a second deploy
The health check rejects the new schema
PM2 refuses to restart
qa.why: The deploy deliberately avoids --force so it cannot delete rows.

qa.q: Why is the login rate limiter unreliable across restarts?
qa.right: It lives in process memory and resets when PM2 restarts the app
wrong: It is stored in a cookie
It is stored in a file that is deployed
It depends on the Cloudflare cache
qa.why: That is fine for one PM2 process but is not durable.

qa.q: Two deploys are started at once. What happens to the second?
qa.right: It fails straight away because the first holds the deploy lock
wrong: It waits and then runs
It cancels the first
It runs in parallel on a copy
qa.why: deploy.sh takes a lock so only one deploy runs at a time.

qa.q: A manager tries to offboard another admin. What happens?
qa.right: It is refused; managers can offboard only learners
wrong: It succeeds after a confirmation
It succeeds but the admin keeps access
It asks the admin to approve
qa.why: Admins can offboard anyone except themselves.

qa.q: A career step names a track whose questions stop at level 8. A rung needs level 10 on it. What happens?
qa.right: It shows as coming soon and never blocks the promotion
wrong: It blocks the promotion until level 10 exists
It is counted as failed
The rung is removed from the ladder
qa.why: Steps the questions cannot reach are not countable.

qa.q: Everything on a rung is met but the person has an overdue required track. What follows?
qa.right: Promotion is on hold unless an admin overrides with a reason
wrong: Promotion happens automatically
A manager can promote without a reason
The overdue track is ignored for promotion
qa.why: Promotion needs required learning not overdue.

qa.q: A person has met 5 of 8 passable steps for the next level. What sub-level are they at?
qa.right: The .1 sub-level
wrong: The .0 sub-level
The .2 sub-level
None; steps do not set a sub-level
qa.why: Half or more met is .1; three quarters or more is .2; fewer than half is .0.

qa.q: A rival's XP is 3,000. What level does the rival show?
qa.why: Level is XP divided by 150, which gives 20.

qa.q: A file imported with status review is run twice. What is the result?
qa.right: Items are matched by track and title and questions by track, level and prompt, so nothing is duplicated
wrong: Every question is duplicated at a shifted level
The track is wiped and reloaded
The questions become active the second time
qa.why: import:knowledge is idempotent.

qa.q: A company policy wording changes but its meaning does not. How do you record it so nobody is asked to re-read?
qa.right: Record it as a non-material wording fix
wrong: Delete and recreate the knowledge item
Add a changeNote and ask everyone to confirm
Retire all linked questions
qa.why: Wording fixes are recorded but ask nobody.

qa.q: A learner joins a track after a material change was recorded. Are they asked to read it?
qa.right: No, because only people enrolled before the change are asked
wrong: Yes, within 7 days
Yes, before they can start
Only if they are a manager
qa.why: Someone who joined later learned the current text from the start.

qa.q: A team wants a client to take the getting-started track but not see staff tracks. What do you set?
qa.right: The person's audience to customer, with the brands or projects they bought
wrong: Their role to learner only
A mandatory tier on the staff tracks
A job role of customer
qa.why: Customers see only tracks whose audience is customer or both.

qa.q: A new track has only 30 questions at levels 1 and 2 and its required level is 5. What does required learning do with it?
qa.right: Leaves it out, because nobody can be required to pass what cannot be taken
wrong: Makes it required anyway and shows it as overdue
Requires level 2 instead
Marks it mandatory
qa.why: Tracks that cannot reach the required level are not counted.

qa.q: Someone says a customer is seeing a staff-only track through a direct link. Where is audience enforced?
qa.right: At enrolment, journeys, contests and the track page
wrong: Only on the dashboard
Only in the Apache config
Only in the invite email
qa.why: The audience check is applied in all those places.

qa.q: A visitor sends a forged X-Forwarded-For header to dodge rate limiting. Which two measures defend against it?
qa.right: Reading the address from the end of the header by TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS and allowing only Cloudflare to reach Apache
wrong: Hashing the header with SHA-256 and storing it in a cookie
Rejecting any request with more than one forwarded address
Using the browser's user agent as the key
qa.why: The real client sits TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS entries from the end, and the allow-list stops direct access.

qa.q: Login takes noticeably longer for registered emails than for unknown ones. What is wrong?
qa.right: The unknown-account path must also pay for a hash so timing does not reveal which emails exist
wrong: Nothing; faster responses for unknown emails are expected
The session version must be bumped
The rate limit is too strict
qa.why: Unknown or offboarded accounts still pay for a hash.

qa.q: A new hire's invite email never arrives. What is the likely reason?
qa.right: The code has no mailer, so the admin must copy the join link and deliver it
wrong: Invites are delivered only by SMS
Email invites are held for 24 hours
The role was entered in upper case
qa.why: No email is sent by the application.

qa.q: A goal's route no longer exists after a ladder edit. What should the person do?
qa.right: Ask an admin about career bridges or pick another goal
wrong: Wait for the route to recreate itself
Pass the track again
Ask the manager to override a promotion
qa.why: The journey shows the route is unreachable and offers to remove the goal.

qa.q: A re-run of import:questions on a track that already has questions adds duplicates. What is the safe way?
qa.right: Clear the track's questions first, then import
wrong: Run it again with --activate
Run seed:careers
Increase the weight of the questions
qa.why: Re-running adds duplicates at shifted levels.

qa.q: Which practice strengthens memory more: rereading notes or testing yourself?
qa.right: Testing yourself, because retrieval practice strengthens recall
wrong: Rereading, because familiarity builds recall
Both equally, since memory is fixed
Neither; only sleep helps
qa.why: Retrieval practice beats rereading.

qa.q: A team wants to release code to production but keep the feature hidden until the launch day. What helps?
qa.right: A feature flag
wrong: A rollback
A hotfix branch
A longer deploy lock
qa.why: A flag separates release from launch.

qa.q: A question is answered correctly by nearly every learner. What does an item analysis suggest?
qa.right: It may be too easy and worth reviewing or retiring
wrong: It is the best question in the bank
It must be moved to a higher level
It should be given a larger weight
qa.why: Questions never failed or nearly always failed are flagged for review.

qa.q: A backup job reports success every night. What is the safest next step?
qa.right: Rehearse restoring it onto a copy
wrong: Trust it since the job reports success
Delete older backups to save space
Run it more often
qa.why: Only a restore test proves the backup works.

qa.q: A script that seeds content is run twice by mistake. What property makes that safe?
qa.right: Idempotency
wrong: Rate limiting
Least privilege
Throttling
qa.why: Each seed step is additive and safe to repeat.

qa.q: An exam has a high pass rate and consistent scores, but graduates do not perform on the job. Which is likely missing?
qa.right: Validity: it may not measure the job skill it claims to
wrong: Reliability: the results are inconsistent
Weighting: the questions need larger weights
A higher pass mark
qa.why: Consistent scores do not prove the test measures the right thing.
